products.name: Weights & Biases
products.note: ML experiment tracking, model registry, and artifact lineage; W&B Weave adds LLM and agent tracing, evaluation, and guardrails; acquired by CoreWeave

reading.body:
Weights & Biases provides ML experiment tracking and LLM tracing tools that help developers monitor what happens during AI training and inference, making it essential infrastructure for understanding and controlling model behavior at scale.

The company occupies a critical position in the AI stack between raw compute and deployed models. Its core function, experiment tracking and artifact lineage, addresses a fundamental problem: as model training consumes more power and compute resources, engineers need visibility into whether that consumption is producing useful progress. Without this layer, scaling becomes blind. The addition of LLM tracing and evaluation tools extends this further into production, where guardrails and monitoring become constraints on how quickly systems can be deployed.

The acquisition by CoreWeave signals consolidation between infrastructure layers. CoreWeave operates data centers and compute resources. The combination suggests that tracking and compute provisioning are moving toward integration, potentially tightening feedback loops between what developers learn about their models and how they allocate infrastructure to train them next.

The data does not reveal customer concentration, revenue, or the scale at which the platform operates. It also does not show whether Weights & Biases' tools themselves are compute-intensive to run, or how they might constrain deployment speed versus enable it. The California law exposure count is noted without context, leaving the nature and severity of those cases unknown.

profile_text.body:
Weights & Biases describes itself as an AI developer platform, and says thousands of companies use it as a system of record for training AI models and developing AI applications. The company was founded in 2017 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its site states that the platform is certified under ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, and ISO/IEC 27018:2019, is compliant with SOC 2 and HIPAA standards, helps customers comply with NIST 800-53, and is aligned with GDPR requirements for processing personal information.

Its tracked product is also named Weights & Biases, covering machine learning experiment tracking, model registry, and artifact lineage. W&B Weave adds LLM and agent tracing, evaluation, and guardrails. The product entry notes that the company was acquired by CoreWeave. A customer quoted on the site says adding a library to their code gave them information about the GenAI portion of their product inside Weights & Biases, which they were already using, and that they can report on AI performance quickly with Weave.

On litigation, no cases are recorded for the company. A California law exposure count of 281 is recorded. No MCP servers are listed.
